terms.grammar: genitive of quis; plural quōrum, quārum
evidence: Plaut. Truc. 604–605: unde es? cujus es?
terms.comment: The plain form. “Whose” in a statement (“the man whose house …”) is the relative: see “which” (relative).

terms.grammar: interrogative adjective, first and second declension
terms.register: vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; Verg. E.
terms.comment: Most frequent in Plautus and Terence (Lewis & Short); Vergil gives it to his herdsmen.

phrases.english: tell me, Damoetas, whose flock is this?
speak up: where are you from? whose are you?
